velden.kop: Video from Kyiv does not show a boy being freed from a torture cellar
velden.oordeel_zin: The footage is genuine, but the boy fell from a wall onto National Guard premises during a protest; no torture cellar was found there [1] [2] [3].
velden.bewering: Remember the face of this 14-year-old who was pulled out of an Azov torture chamber near Kiev.
velden.kort: Since the evening of 2 November, a video and a photo of a boy in a grey blanket have been circulating in Dutch, claiming he was freed from a Ukrainian torture cellar near Kyiv [13]. The footage is genuine and comes from a protest at a National Guard house in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka, on the edge of Kyiv [2] [3]. The 14-year-old climbed onto the wall during that protest and fell onto the premises; he was not held there [1] [3].
velden.tekst:
A National Guard unit used the house as temporary quarters for mobilised men waiting for their training [2] [4]. On 2 November, a claim spread online that armed men were holding and torturing some 40 people in a cellar there. The police called this false the same afternoon [5]. Even so, a crowd came to the site, and in the evening eggs, bottles and stones were thrown at the police and the National Guard [3].

A reporter for The Kyiv Independent saw the boy climb into a tree and onto the wall, shout abuse at the soldiers, throw stones and then fall from the wall onto the premises [3]. According to the Ukrainian State Service for Children, he lives nearby, came to the protest after school and fell when people began shaking the fence [1]. Inside, he was wrapped in a blanket. His sister picked him up that evening, and he was admitted to the Kyiv children's hospital, not in danger of his life [1]. That departure is what the video shows: a boy in a blanket being led away through the crowd.

No torture cellar has been found. A veteran who entered the house that evening told the investigative outlet Slidstvo.Info that he saw no places of torture [2]. The rumour came from a woman in an ambulance uniform, who said she ran an ambulance service. That service has not operated since 2023 [2] [4]. The police arrested her on 3 November and speak of a planned provocation [6].

In Dutch, the video was already on X on 2 November at 22:25, with the claim that the boy had been tortured with a shovel [13]. A day later, the Russian embassy in the Netherlands shared the same footage in English [12]. VRT NWS called the claim false on 5 November, and AFP Factcheck Nederland followed on 12 November [10] [11].
velden.niet_weten: Whether violence was used in the house is not yet clear. In a video of his own, the boy says he was beaten inside; the Minister of the Interior denies this [1] [9]. Soldiers who stayed there complained to the military ombudsman about beatings, and the State Bureau of Investigation is looking into it [7] [8]. That does not change what the video shows: a boy who fell inside during the protest, not a prisoner being freed. Whether Russia steered the protest has also not been established; Russian networks did amplify the story afterwards [14].
